sections.h2: Who sends and collects the property tax bill in Colquitt County, Georgia?
sections.html:
The Colquitt County Tax Commissioner bills and collects the tax, while the Tax Assessor's Office sets the value. The tax commissioner's own site says the office does not set value or the millage rate, so a complaint about the size of a bill belongs with the assessors and the elected boards that levy the rate.

The tax commissioner's office is at 101 East Central Ave. in Moultrie, with a mailing box at P.O. Box 99, Moultrie, GA 31768. Its posted hours are Monday through Friday, 8:00am to 4:30pm, and the property tax line is (229) 616-7410. The county commission and the county Board of Education each levy a millage rate, and the Board of Equalization, appointed by the grand jury, hears value appeals.

  • Tax Assessor's Office: appraises property, mails assessment notices, approves exemptions.
  • Board of Equalization: hears administrative appeals of those values.
  • County commission and school board: set the mill rate that turns value into a bill.
  • Tax Commissioner: mails the bill, takes payment, records liens.

sections.h2: What should a Moultrie-area seller know about Colquitt County itself?
sections.html:
Colquitt County sits in Southwest Georgia, covers about 557 square miles, and has Moultrie as its county seat and largest city. The county was created on February 25, 1856, and Wikipedia lists Tift, Cook, Brooks, Thomas, Mitchell and Worth counties as its neighbors.

Moultrie is an agricultural city about 24 miles west of Interstate 75, and US 319 links it to I-75 and I-10. The Colquitt County School District serves the county, and Moultrie also has a Southern Regional Technical College campus, an Abraham Baldwin Agricultural College campus and a medical school campus. For a seller, the practical point is that many parcels here are farm tracts, rural lots and older town houses, and a tract with timber or crops may carry a different tax treatment than a plain house lot.

The Census Bureau's QuickFacts page shows 47,438 residents in its July 2025 estimate and 19,775 housing units. Roughly 63.7% of homes are owner-occupied, the median owner-occupied value for 2020 to 2024 is $121,400, and median gross rent is $818. Median household income over the same period is $49,341. Those are countywide figures, so a street in Moultrie can sit well above or below them.

sections.h2: When are Colquitt County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Real estate and business personal property taxes in Colquitt County are normally due December 10. The tax commissioner's bill page adds that bills go out at least 60 days before the due date, and that the date printed on your bill controls if it differs.

If December 10 lands on a weekend or holiday, the office accepts payment on the next business day. A mailed check must be postmarked by the due date to avoid interest, and the office asks you to include the payment stub or write the bill number on the check. Mobile and manufactured homes run on a separate schedule and the county's own pages disagree on the date, so ask the tax commissioner which deadline applies to your home before you rely on either one.

  • Bills go to the owner of record on January 1 of the tax year.
  • The office cannot guarantee that a bill reaches you, and interest still runs if it does not.
  • Bills are mailed to the owner, never to the mortgage company, so forward yours to a lender that does not escrow.

sections.h2: What happens if Colquitt County property tax goes unpaid?
sections.html:
Interest starts after the due date, a penalty can follow, and the tax commissioner can record a lien called a FiFa. The office says it treats levy and sale as a last resort, but unpaid property may be levied upon and ultimately sold.

The county's pages describe the FiFa as going on the General Execution Docket at the Clerk of Superior Court, where credit bureaus can read it. The site states the lien stays on a credit record for at least seven years. The penalty is not applied to homesteaded property with a bill under $500, and the office says it mails delinquent notices only at certain intervals, so verify the exact payoff with the office rather than trusting an old notice.

Because the interest and penalty descriptions on the site do not match each other, request a written payoff figure for the day you plan to pay or close.

sections.h2: Who owes the Colquitt County tax when a house sells?
sections.html:
The person who owned the house on January 1 is the one named on the bill and, if it stays unpaid, on the lien. Selling in March or October does not change that on the county's books.

Georgia law, as the tax commissioner explains it, records the lien in the January 1 owner's name unless the office receives a contract or closing statement within 90 days of the due date showing the buyer took responsibility. If your closing prorated the tax, carry a copy of the settlement statement to the office at 101 East Central Ave. inside that window. The office will then record any lien against the new owner instead.

If a bill arrives for a house you already sold, forward it to the new owner. A buyer's title company usually handles the split at closing, and a seller who wants a clean exit should still ask the title company how it will pay the county.

sections.h2: Which homestead exemptions does Colquitt County list?
sections.html:
The tax commissioner's site lists a standard exemption plus several age, income and veteran exemptions, all deducted from the assessed value, which Georgia sets at 40% of fair market value. The application goes to the Tax Assessor's Office, and it must be received by April 1 of the first year you claim it. A later application counts for the following year.

  • Standard homestead: listed as $2,000 off the assessed value for the county, school system and state levies, not the bond portion.
  • Elderly school tax: age 62 or older, net income not over $10,000, up to $10,000 off for school tax.
  • Elderly general: age 65 or older, applicant and spouse income not over $10,000, up to $4,000 off.
  • Disabled veteran and qualifying surviving spouse: up to $63,780 off.
  • Floating exemption: age 62 or older, gross household income of $30,000 or less, state and county tax only.

Once granted, a homestead renews itself each year until you move, the ownership changes or you want a different exemption. The county also has local exemptions that override the state amount when larger, so ask the assessors for today's numbers. Two further relief paths exist: a deferral for owners 62 and older with gross household income of $15,000 or less, and the 30% agricultural assessment for qualifying farmland.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Colquitt County assessment?
sections.html:
File within 45 days of the date on the assessment notice. The county's FAQ says you may appeal to the Board of Equalization or to an arbitrator, and a decision from either can be carried on to Superior Court by written notice to the Board of Tax Assessors.

Georgia also lets you file a return between January 1 and April 1 stating your own opinion of the property's value. If the assessors change that value, you keep appeal rights. Mailing address changes matter too, since the law sends notices to your last known address.

Mobile home owners who disagree with the value have 45 days to appeal to the Board of Tax Assessors, and the county page then gives 21 days from the notice to go on to the Board of Equalization.

A seller with back taxes or a recorded lien can still sell, as long as the payoff is settled at the closing table. Ask the tax commissioner for the figure early, then set it against what the sale will bring.

faqs.q: What is the Colquitt County property tax due date?
faqs.a: December 10 for real estate and business personal property, according to the tax commissioner's site. Check the date printed on your own bill, because the office says it can change.

faqs.q: Does selling in the middle of the year move the tax to the buyer?
faqs.a: Not on the county's books. The January 1 owner stays on the bill and any lien unless the office receives a closing statement within 90 days of the due date showing the buyer accepted the tax.

faqs.q: When must a homestead application be filed in Colquitt County?
faqs.a: By April 1 of the year you first claim it. The Tax Assessor's Office takes the application, and a first-time owner should bring a copy of the warranty deed.

faqs.q: How long do I have to challenge my Colquitt County value?
faqs.a: 45 days from the date of the assessment notice. You choose the Board of Equalization or an arbitrator, and a further appeal to Superior Court is possible afterward.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Colquitt County house that has a tax lien?
faqs.a: Yes. The lien is paid from the sale proceeds at closing, so ask the tax commissioner for a payoff figure and give it to the title company before the closing date.
